pendingIdeas.title: Check every listing thirty days after submission for edits, expiry and a live link
pendingIdeas.description: Directories silently truncate descriptions, change categories and drop listings when a free period ends. Work: build a small register of each submission with the date, the URL, the fields submitted and the next check date, then run the first thirty-day check and record what changed. Deliver the register, the first check results, the two listings that need correcting, and the cadence that keeps them accurate without monthly effort.

upvotes.reason: "Check every listing thirty days after submission for edits, expiry and a live link" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it produces something checkable rather than an opinion, so the goal either moved or it did not.

pendingIdeas.title: Keep a negative list: the directories that rank competitors beside you or hide you behind a paid tier
pendingIdeas.description: Not every index is a shop window; some are comparison pages where Zedu appears as the cheaper, less-known option next to established tools. Work: for each candidate, record how listings are ordered, whether sponsored placement pushes free listings down, and whether the page targets "alternative" searches against a competitor. Deliver the negative list with the reason per entry, and the criteria that would let a future submission reverse each decision.

pendingIdeas.title: Record what each directory does with your contact details, not only what it charges to list
pendingIdeas.description: The real cost of a free listing is often a sales pipeline you did not ask for: lead resale, a required demo, a stream of vendor calls. Work: for each shortlisted directory, record the submission form fields, the terms on lead sharing, whether the listing is visible without a paid tier, and what happened to the contact address afterwards. Deliver the cost-and-consequence table, the two directories to skip for that reason, and the alias or role address to use where the form demands a work email.

upvotes.reason: "Record what each directory does with your contact details, not only what it charges to list" has a scriptable structure, so it can be produced and reviewed rather than left open-ended. it produces something checkable rather than an opinion, so the goal either moved or it did not.

pendingIdeas.title: Tag the link in every listing and cut the ones that send nobody after sixty days
pendingIdeas.description: A directory that sends no visitor is a page maintained for nothing. Work: give each listing a tagged destination so referral traffic and sign-ups can be attributed, set the sixty-day decision point, and define what counts as worth keeping (one qualified enquiry, not just a click). Deliver the tagging scheme, the reporting view, the sixty-day rule, and the first read of which directories are already sending traffic without attribution.

upvotes.reason: "Tag the link in every listing and cut the ones that send nobody after sixty days" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.

Most directory work stops at "submitted" and never checks whether the link sends anyone. Tagging each listing and cutting the ones that send nothing after sixty days turns a list of submissions into a measured channel, and it is the only part of this goal that reports a result.

pendingIdeas.title: Write two listing descriptions, because a school buyer and a bootcamp buyer search with different words
pendingIdeas.description: One generic profile wastes the only field that matters. Work: write an education-institution variant (safeguarding, departments, timetables, procurement) and a bootcamp variant (cohorts, mentors, demo day, placement), each within the platform's character limits, using only product facts. Deliver both versions with their limits respected, the keyword choices each one makes, and the note on which claims were removed because the live product does not support them.

upvotes.reason: On the pages this goal is about, "Write two listing descriptions, because a school buyer and a bootcamp buyer search with different words" is the kind of fix that can be verified against the live site after delivery, so it either moved the number or it did not. it produces something checkable rather than an opinion, so the goal either moved or it did not.

The same listing copy cannot serve both buyers: a school buyer searches for safeguarding and class structure, a bootcamp buyer for cohorts and speed. Writing two versions per directory is small, specific work that a submission task can use directly.
